qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-01-stricter-r2/runtime-results.json:fact inventory and inspected raw evidence portions
evidence: Most public feature groups have real implementations and hash-bound scripted support (see evidence/17/deliverable-map.json). Verified all 60 index hashes, all 15 frozen solution files against full installation, and all 80 coverage keys against actual passing raw fact entries; none is treated as a configured grade or exhaustive input proof. Independent browser probes on isolated cw-h2-row17 with exact frozen solution show two gaps. (1) overview.md:5 asks for complete HTML documents; behaviour.md:11 asks for interactive controls; security.md:5 supports ordinary source-written functions/DOM changes. In solution/app/src/runtime.ts:330-334 each on* attribute generates a fresh id and overwrites the same data-cw-handler attribute. An ordinary button with onclick and onkeydown therefore fails during Run with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading addEventListener) ? line 1', retaining the previous picture; one inline handler succeeds. (2) behaviour.md:25 says 'Loading should bring back the title, filename and source unchanged.' server.js:44 trims accepted filename text. UI Save of filename '  leading.js' leaves that exact filename shown as saved, but browser reload/load gives 'leading.js'; the server's stored record already has the trimmed value. This is a bounded additional P2 fidelity defect. Raw cases: evidence/17/probe-results.json; positive native and equivalent two-addEventListener controls: evidence/17/alternative-results.json. Both controls produce clicked then keyed, with the app alternative completing. Own runtime hashes and /tmp working directory are recorded in evidence/17/isolated-runtime-binding.json. No provider/Oracle/portal score is claimed.
counterexample: Broken app that can look covered: the frozen reference itself maps to all 80 existing raw functional observations yet rejects <html><body><button onclick="this.textContent='clicked'" onkeydown="this.textContent='keyed'">Two handlers</button></body></html> in two.html and silently changes accepted '  leading.js' on save/reload. Successful controls prove the ordinary operations work: one inline handler, native HTML with both handlers, and equivalent app HTML using two addEventListener calls all work. Conforming alternative considered: preserving one element identity for both instrumented handlers (or correctly handling both original attributes) and storing the exact accepted filename would satisfy the public outcomes; no particular marker scheme or API is required. The current scripted scenarios do not establish completeness for those alternatives/boundaries.
suggested_fix: Use one stable marker per HTML element for all rewritten handlers, preserve the exact accepted filename when saving and snapshotting, rebuild the delivered bundle, and rerun focused positive/negative controls plus affected recovery/history checks in a new candidate.
